items.narrative:
This audit covers 50 traceability events recorded between 2025-02-05 and 2025-06-15, drawn from 12 source sheets spanning harvesting, cooling, packing, receiving, transformation, and shipping. Of the 17 products in scope, 5 are definitively on the Food Traceability List, 9 are classified as suspicious and require formal determination, and only 3 are confirmed off-list. The 50 events break down to 19 shipping and 4 transformation critical tracking events, with no external trading partners recorded and 0 internal transfer events logged.

The most severe gap is lot integrity: 13 events have backward lineage gaps, meaning the chain of custody cannot be traced back to origin for the majority of lots — a fundamental traceability failure. Five findings are rated high severity, and 61 are rated medium, for a total of 66 findings. Scope and exemption uncertainty accounts for 42 of those findings, reflecting that the business has not formally resolved which products are subject to traceability requirements. All 19 shipping events have unknown destinations, meaning there is no recorded receiving-party information for any outbound shipment. Key data element coverage stands at 84.44%, with 7 missing out of 45 graded, and 5 inbound ERP mismatches indicate that records entering the system do not consistently match source documents. A traceability plan finding and 3 GS1 requirement findings round out the picture of systemic recordkeeping gaps.

The immediate priority is resolving the 13 backward lineage gaps — start by pulling the 2 linked lots as a reference model and working backward through the 4 transformation events to reconstruct input-output lot connections. The 9 suspicious products must be formally classified against the Food Traceability List before any other remediation is meaningful; until that is done, 42 scope-uncertainty findings cannot be closed. Fix the unknown destination problem on all 19 shipping events by requiring a confirmed trading partner identifier at the point of dispatch, and address the 5 inbound ERP mismatches by reconciling the Goods In and Dock Landings sheets against source purchase orders. Finally, complete the traceability plan document flagged in the findings and correct the 3 GS1 requirement gaps identified in the Item Catalog and related records.
